rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06130] Its `beforeEach` now does `resetToastInteractionForTests()` (order independence) plus a real `window.dispatchEvent(new Event("pointerdown"))` that reaches the actual capture-phase listener, while the audio mock still offers only `playAudio`.

nodes.label: The user-interaction latch lives in ToastSound.tsx, not utils/audio.ts
nodes.norm_label: the user-interaction latch lives in toastsound.tsx, not utils/audio.ts
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06128] Keeping the latch in `ToastSound.tsx` means the toast path reads exactly one thing from `utils/audio` (`playAudio`), before and after the change, so the negative control needed no structural rescue at all. It is also the more honest location: this is a toast-cue rule, not a general audio rule, and putting it in `utils/audio` would invite a future reader to think it applies to `playAudio`.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L02376] But the negative control is a hard constraint: "Do not remove, skip, or weaken any existing test, including the negative control." If I put it in utils/audio and ToastSound reads `hasUserInteracted`, the negative control MUST fail. So B it is.

nodes.label: Capture-phase, passive, module-load interaction listener
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06132] Listener: capture-phase, passive, on `pointerdown` / `keydown` / `touchstart`, registered at module load (not in an effect, so the latch is armed before the first background toast can fire), guarded by `typeof window !== "undefined" && typeof window.addEventListener === "function"`. Capture matters: a bubble-phase handler calling `stopPropagation()` must not be able to raise a toast before the latch flips. `touchstart` is kept because a webview that has not synthesised pointer events still delivers it, and it is idempotent otherwise.

nodes.label: A PCSX2 .ps2 memory card file is 16384 sectors of 528 bytes, mapped 1:1 onto card address
nodes.norm_label: a pcsx2 .ps2 memory card file is 16384 sectors of 528 bytes, mapped 1:1 onto card address
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09532] **Card size**: `McdSizeInSectors = m_fileSize / (SectorSize + EraseBlockSizeInSectors)` = 8650752 / (512 + 16) = 8650752 / 528 = 16384.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09530] 1. **`Seek` is a raw 1:1 file seek** — `FSeek64(f, adr, SEEK_SET)`. So **card address == file offset**. The data is at file offset 0, NOT 0x40000. My assumption was wrong.

nodes.label: PCSX2 never writes per-sector checksums into a .ps2 memory card file; the bytes stay at the 0xFF fill
nodes.norm_label: pcsx2 never writes per-sector checksums into a .ps2 memory card file; the bytes stay at the 0xff fill
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09766] So the per-sector XOR checksum is simply **not present** in PCSX2's file format. The checksum bytes are 0xFF (the fill value from `Create()`), never updated.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09845] Data 最新 menunjukkan byte checksum sector semuanya `0xFF` — itu **fill value** dari `Create()` (`MemoryCardFile.cpp:389-396`), artinya PCSX2 memang **tidak pernah menulis** checksum per-sector ke file. Jadi angka "16317 beda" itu **nihil**, bukan bukti rusak.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09768] The guest BIOS (mcman/mcserv) computes checksums on the fly during transfer, not reading them from the file.
